This weak tornado orginally began as a waterspout over Copano Bay. The tornado dissipated shortly after making landfall.
The Aransas Wildlife Refuge reported hail ranging from the size of quarters to golfballs. Multiple funnel clouds and excessive cloud to ground lightning was also reported.
Damage was confined to power lines blown down north of Aransas Pass, along Highway 35.
Straight-line winds ripped the patio roof off the bait shop at the Fin and Feather RV park. Two power poles were knocked down and a vehicle was damaged in the parking lot.

An NWS survey team concluded a tornado touched down 4 miles west of Rockport. The tornado was on the ground for roughly 3.75 miles, traveling southeast and ending near Bypass 35 and 16th streets. The maximum wind speed was estimated at 120 mph, an EF-2, and had a maximum width of…
At the Cove Harbor Marina signs were snapped and roofs partially damaged. Several power lines and trees were reported downed throughout the city of Rockport.

A NWS Storm Survey confirmed a tornado touched down just outside of Goose Island State Park and moved southwest into the park. Medium to large tree limbs were snapped along a roughly 1/2 mile track. Winds were estimated to be 65 mph. This tornado occurred in the outer rainbands o…
A tornado briefly touched down near the intersection of 9th Street and Business 35. Windows were blown out of the Kimco Business. This tornado occurred in the outer rainbands of Hurricane Alex.

Wood roof and awning of home blown completely off. Part of the roof blown into roof of nearby house. One snapped tree limb blown through wall of house. Roof damage and trees uprooted along a two mile path from Live Oak Elementary school to the intersection of Nopal and Austin Str…

NWS Storm survey determined straight-line winds struck a narrow corridor in Fulton between Farm to Market Road 3036 and West Mesquite Street. The winds caused widespread tree damage. A mobile home lost its roof and a metal storage building partially collapsed along Farm to Market…

NWS storm survey determined straight-line winds of approximately 70 to 80 mph struck Belaire Drive in Holiday Beach. The roof was blown off of one home which impacted 2 other homes and caused extensive damage.
NWS storm survey concluded a weak tornado touched down in rural Aransas County northeast of Holiday Beach. The tornado crossed Highway 35 snapping one telephone pole.
Spotter reported quarter sized hail southwest of Rockport.
Golf ball sized hail was reported on the southwest side of Rockport.
Observer reported nickel sized hail occurred at the headquarters of the Aransas National Wildlife Refuge.
TCOON site on Aransas National Wildlife Refuge recorded a 67 mph wind gust.
Power poles were blown down southwest of Rockport.
A small wooden building was destroyed near the pharmacy.
Roof damage occurred to a home along Rattlesnake Point Road near Rockport.
Roofing of a screened-in porch of a house along the bay was ripped off and flipped onto the house. The porch framing was damaged and collapsed.
A front porch and roof were damaged at a house on Jacoby Lane.
Ping pong ball sized hail occurred near Sparks Colony Drive west of Rockport.
NOS site in Rockport measured a gust to 51 knots.
Several people were trapped in an overturned trailer.
Video submitted through social media showed tennis ball sized hail in Holiday Beach.
Video was submitted through social media of quarter to half dollar sized hail at Goose Island State Park. Hail covered the ground.
Golf ball sized hail occurred in Lamar.
Tornado touched down on Belaire Drive removing the roof from one home with debris blown into another home across the street. Several power poles were snapped.
Storm spotter measured a 62 mph wind gust in Rockport.
Quarter sized hail occurred in Rockport.
Aransas County ASOS measured a gust to 59 mph.
Public report of weather station recording a wind gust to 64 mph west of Rockport.
Rockport/Aransas County Municipal Airport measured a gust to 51 knots.
